disposition_mapping.rationale: Claim submission is retained as the employee-initiated action, now merged with the data-extraction function since OCR runs synchronously at submission time rather than in a separate downstream step.

Receipt capture and data extraction is automated and folded into the submission interface (OCR at point of capture), removing the manual AP-analyst handling while preserving the structured claim record output.

Policy compliance check survives as a mandatory gate (EXR-R-07) but is restructured from a manual AP-analyst check into an automated rules-engine pass that flags exceptions, still completing before manager approval (EXR-R-02).

Line manager approval is retained unchanged in function and actor (EXR-R-08), occurring after the policy check and before reimbursement (EXR-R-06), and remains a distinct actor from the submitter (EXR-R-03).

Finance review persists but is restructured to a risk-targeted exception review, driven by the policy exception flags produced upstream, preserving the evidential trail required by KB-02 without re-reviewing every clean claim.

Posting is retained with its mandatory inputs of transaction date (EXR-R-04) and transaction-date exchange rate (EXR-R-05) unchanged, consistent with IAS 21 translation requirements (KB-07) and period cutoff discipline (KB-03).

Reimbursement via the AP payment run survives as required (EXR-R-09), still occurring after line manager approval (EXR-R-06), and is merged with the notification function since payment-completion events can trigger notification automatically.

Employee notification is unconstrained by design and is absorbed into the payment-run step as an automated system trigger fired on payment confirmation, removing the separate manual notification task.

steps.description: The employee submits an out-of-pocket expense claim via a mobile/web capture tool that performs OCR data extraction at the point of submission, populating a structured claim record in real time. Receipts for claim lines above the receipt threshold are mandatory attachments; the system blocks submission if they are missing.
inputs: Receipts for claim lines above the receipt threshold
steps.name: Claim submission with automated receipt capture

steps.description: A rules engine checks every claim line against expense policy limits, categories and per diem rates immediately after submission. Compliant claims are auto-flagged clean; non-compliant or exception lines (e.g. missing receipt waivers, over-limit amounts) are flagged for finance exception review. This is a mandatory, non-bypassable gate that must complete before manager approval.
steps.name: Automated policy compliance check

steps.description: The claimant's line manager approves or rejects the policy-checked claim, with policy exception flags surfaced for visibility. The approver is necessarily distinct from the claim submitter.
steps.name: Line manager approval

steps.description: Finance reviews only the subset of approved claims carrying policy exception flags, coding anomalies, or evidentiary gaps; clean claims pass straight through without manual finance touch. This preserves the evidential/faithful-representation check (KB-02) on a risk-targeted basis rather than reviewing every line.
steps.name: Finance exception review

steps.description: The claim is posted to expense accounts and cost centres in the period the expense was incurred, with foreign-currency lines translated at the transaction-date spot rate per IAS 21 (KB-07). Exchange differences arising on settlement are tracked and reported separately rather than netted (KB-08), preserving period cutoff discipline (KB-03).
steps.name: Posting

steps.description: The approved, posted claim is paid to the employee through the AP payment run; recognition of the liability and its derecognition on payment remain separately determinable (KB-11). On successful payment, the system automatically notifies the employee of reimbursement, eliminating the separate manual notification step.
steps.name: Reimbursement via AP payment run with automated notification
